o.norm: tests that the pretty printer does not collapse (trim leading | trailing whitespace) when there are sequential textnodes. That doesn't happen in a parse, but can when manipulated. needs to be text that would indent

i.norm:
Verifies that the pretty printer does NOT collapse (i.e. trim leading/trailing whitespace) when two text nodes sit next to each other as siblings.

A normal parse never produces two adjacent text nodes, but DOM manipulation (such as inserting a node after an existing text node) can. In that situation the printer must keep the whitespace between the two fragments so the rendered text stays readable.
Parse a <div> that contains an empty nested <div> followed by the text "Hello". The text needs to be content that the pretty printer would normally indent.
childNode(1) is the "Hello" text node (childNode(0) is the empty nested <div>).
Manually insert a second, adjacent text node right after "Hello". This creates the sequential-text-node scenario that a parse alone cannot.
The two text nodes remain separate and retain their exact whitespace.
The combined, normalized text reads as a single sentence.
Pretty-printed HTML: the adjacent text nodes are joined without collapsing the space between them.
